To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• the mutation-based criterion is more ‘difficult’ to satisfy than the data flow criterion. • the cost of achieving the mutation-based criterion (in terms of number of test cases) is higher than the cost of achieving data flow adequacy. • a test set consisting entirely of mutation-based test cases is not necessarily a better test set than a test set consisting only of data flow-based test cases. • the mutation-based approach is a useful tool in software testing.
the mutation criterion is more difficult to satisfy than the all-uses criterion, but that satisfying the mutation criterion costs less than satisfying the all-uses criteria.
the mutation based criterion is more difficult to satisfy, and is more expensive to satisfy than the data flow based criterion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the empirical evaluation of the data flow all-uses criterion in the context of mutation testing.
the empirical comparison of two test criteria, the data flow and mutation criteria.
comparing the ‘difficulty’ and cost of two test adequacy criteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mutation-based criterion is more difficult than the data flow based criterion and is more expensive.
the data flow based approach is better than the mutation based one.
the all-uses criterion is a better test adequacy criteria than the mutation based criterion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, for a given test suite of a program, it is easier to satisfy a data-flow based criterion than a mutation-based criterion, and that it is less expensive to satisfy the mutation-based criterion than a data-flow based one.
the mutation-based test adequacy criteria is more ‘difficult to satisfy’ than the data flow-based all-uses criterion.
the mutation based criterion is ‘harder’ to satisfy than the data flow based one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mutation based criteria are more effective than data flow based criteria in detecting errors in programs.
the data flow based criterion is easier to satisfy than the mutation based criterion.
data flow testing is a more difficult and costly approach than mutation-based testing.
